content: The text provided is a list of contributors to the fourth edition of the Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality, incorporating the first and second addenda. Each entry includes the name of the contributor, their affiliation, and their country of representation. Johannesburg Water in South Africa contributed to the guidelines through their expertise in water management. R.C. Neto from the Universidade Federal do Ceará in Brazil provided valuable input based on their academic and research background. T. Neville, representing Vestergaard Frandsen in Zambia, contributed insights into water safety and sanitation. G. Newcombe, formerly associated with SA Water in Australia, shared their expertise in water quality management. T.S.V.F. Ngowi from the Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences in Tanzania contributed their knowledge in public health and water safety. C.H.W. Nieves from Columbia University in the United States provided academic expertise in water-related health issues. Y. Nijdam from Waternet in the Netherlands contributed their technical knowledge in water management systems. C.K. Njoya from the Ministry of Water and Energy in Cameroon provided governmental perspectives on water policy and infrastructure. A. Nocker from the IWW Water Centre in Germany, formerly of Cranfield University in the United Kingdom, shared their expertise in water microbiology. C. Nokes from Environmental Science and Research Ltd in New Zealand contributed their knowledge in environmental health and water safety. V.J. Novotny, Professor Emeritus at Marquette University and Northeastern University in the United States, provided academic insights into water quality and environmental engineering. N. O’Connor from Ecos Environmental Consulting in Australia contributed their expertise in environmental impact assessments. O. Odediran from the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) in the United States provided insights into global water and sanitation initiatives. B. Odugbemi, a consultant at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital in Nigeria, contributed their medical expertise in waterborne diseases. O. Oenema from Wageningen University and Research Center in the Netherlands shared their knowledge in sustainable water management. G. Offringa, formerly of the Water Research Commission in South Africa, contributed their expertise in water research and policy. P.-Y. Oger from UNICEF in the United States provided insights into child health and water safety. M.-E. Oh from Pusan National University in South Korea contributed their academic expertise in water quality. E. Ohanian from the Environmental Protection Agency in the United States provided regulatory perspectives on water safety. K. Ohno, formerly of the National Institute of Public Health in Japan, shared their expertise in public health and water quality. S. Okamoto from the Public Works Research Institute in Japan contributed their technical knowledge in water infrastructure. S. Ólafsdóttir from the Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority in Iceland provided expertise in food safety and water quality. G.N.L. Ong from the National University of Singapore contributed their academic insights into water and environmental health. L. Onyon from the World Health Organization (WHO) in Switzerland provided global perspectives on water safety standards. C.J. Osborne from the University of Queensland in Australia contributed their expertise in water research and management. P.S. Oshida, formerly of the Environmental Protection Agency in the United States, shared their regulatory knowledge in water safety. W. Oswald from the Rollins School of Public Health in the United States provided public health expertise in waterborne diseases. J. O’Toole from Monash University in Australia contributed their academic knowledge in water and environmental health.
